name: St Demetrios the Great-martyr
title: Myrrh-streamer of Thessaloniki
summary: The young governor of Thessaloniki who taught his city about Christ, blessed little Nestor to defeat a giant, and still watches over his city.
sourceNote: The text for older readers follows the Life of St Demetrios in St Dimitri of Rostov's Lives of the Saints (October 26), retold in our own English words. Draft — awaiting review.

teaching.caption: Demetrios, governor of Thessaloniki, teaches the people about Christ.
teaching.alt: The harbor city of Thessaloniki with white houses, a lighthouse and ships with colorful sails. Young Demetrios with a golden halo, wearing a white tunic and red cloak, stands on marble steps holding the Gospel, while men, women and children listen and seagulls fly overhead.

nestor.caption: Young Nestor cries, "God of Demetrios, help me!" and defeats the giant Lyaeus.
nestor.alt: A Roman stadium full of spectators under colorful awnings. Small, brave Nestor, glowing with light, stands on a wooden platform as the enormous gladiator Lyaeus topples backwards. Emperor Maximian watches angrily from his royal box.

protector.caption: St Demetrios appears on a red horse to protect his city of Thessaloniki.
protector.alt: St Demetrios in armor and a red cloak rides a red horse along the walls of Thessaloniki, shining with heavenly light, while frightened enemy soldiers run away and the townspeople on the walls raise their hands in thanksgiving. The sea, ships and the city's churches are in the background.
